answer: Every account in the network keeps a heartbeat. Once per epoch, each vertex must send a signed pulse that quotes a fresh random number published that epoch, and two neighbours must countersign it in time, so a whisper of stale data can never pass for a live one. Building one fake costs a 30-credit deposit on each neighbour edge plus three hours of genuine interaction, and missing a single pulse forfeits 20 credits. A thousand fakes would therefore lock up 60,000 credits, risk 20,000 more each epoch, and collapse the moment a neighbour stops vouching.
